extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven mathematical reasoning types and five primary tasks across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from three sources: (1) nine existing MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples); (2) 19 VQA datasets selected from a review of 70+ datasets using heuristic rules and manual annotation by three expert annotators (2,739 examples); and (3) three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields with a two-step review process (736 examples).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: False positive examples from automatic heuristic filtering were handled by manual labeling by three expert annotators using majority voting. Annotation disagreements (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Nine existing MathQA datasets (GPS, MWP, TQA), 19 publicly available VQA datasets containing math-related instances, puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations (tables, figures, charts) from online education resources and papers on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers for PaperQA were sourced from August 2023; no other specific timeframe is mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Expert annotators labeled problems involving mathematical reasoning using a custom annotation tool. Annotators were trained with detailed instructions and examples (positive and negative). Three labeling options were provided: Yes, No, and Unsure. Annotators could leave comments for incorrect or offensive content. For human performance evaluation, AMT workers with >5,000 HIT tasks and acceptance score >0.99 were used, with qualification questions required.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (for mathematical reasoning labeling) and Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance evaluation
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 was computed among three annotators, indicating substantial inter-annotator agreement
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators for mathematical reasoning labeling; 5 annotators per question for human performance evaluation on testmini
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: AMT workers with a history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks and an acceptance score higher than 0.99
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations were sourced from original data providers with only 85.6% of examples having annotations, and annotations lack a unified format and structure due to heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has limited dataset coverage, with potential gaps in certain mathematical problem types and visual contexts. It focuses on specific domains like science and college-level math, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. The study also focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models, and there is potential data noise.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to advance AI capabilities in mathematical and visual reasoning, contributing to the broader understanding of foundation model limitations and improvements in this domain.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating and benchmarking the mathematical reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in visual contexts, covering tasks such as figure question answering, math word problems, and theorem-based reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitments to maintain the datasets by refining potential data noise based on community feedback, and to evolve the leaderboard in response to new models. Future iterations will encompass broader problems and visual contexts with unified and comprehensive annotations.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Stratified sampling strategy to create testmini subset: first randomly sample questions with a threshold of 4 per source dataset, then randomly sample remaining questions proportionally. KL Divergence and TV distance between testmini and full set are 0.008 and 0.035 respectively.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic selection of mathematical problems using a dictionary of quantity words; quality checks to address unidentified errors; division into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets.

name.evidence: we present MATHVISTA, a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: the dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data... rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: MATHVISTA represents a significant step forward in the field. We are dedicated to continuously improving our benchmark to better understand and enhance the capabilities of AI in mathematical and visual reasoning.
